More to come.Posted on:Jun 26, 2026, 10:46 AM INTEGRAL CALCULUS (MTH_252Z_400_U2026) Front Page Welcome to MTH 252! --> For BOTH Sections 400 and 401 In this course we continue our study of Calculus. More specifically we will study, abstract, and apply the idea of measuring area between two curves. To group the content in a meaningful way, this course is split into five units: Unit 1 - We introduce Riemann sums as a tool to approximate area by summing up the area of rectangles. Unit 2 - We study the Fundamental Theorem of Calculus and related properties, which rely on "undoing" derivatives. Unit 3 - We study a variety of problem-solving techniques in order to apply the Fundamental Theorem of Calculus to more complex settings. Unit 4 - We explore various graphical applications. Unit 5 - We apply our techniques to solve real-world problems. We are very happy to have you in this course and look forward to working with you throughout the quarter! Watch this video that gives an overview of your MTH 252 Canvas course: Course Learning Outcomes By the end of this course, you should be able to: Describe the definite integral as a limit of Riemann sums and illustrate and interpret definite integrals as areas and signed areas. Evaluate integrals using basic numerical integration rules. Apply the fundamental theorem of calculus to evaluate integrals and to differentiate integrals with respect to a limit of integration. Use integration to find areas and volumes of regions and calculate physical quantities such as total distance traveled, displacement, work, and volume. More to come.Posted on:Jun 26, 2026, 10:46 AM INTEGRAL CALCULUS (MTH_252Z_400_U2026) Front Page Welcome to MTH 252! --> For BOTH Sections 400 and 401 In this course we continue our study of Calculus. More specifically we will study, abstract, and apply the idea of measuring area between two curves. To group the content in a meaningful way, this course is split into five units: Unit 1 - We introduce Riemann sums as a tool to approximate area by summing up the area of rectangles. Unit 2 - We study the Fundamental Theorem of Calculus and related properties, which rely on "undoing" derivatives. Unit 3 - We study a variety of problem-solving techniques in order to apply the Fundamental Theorem of Calculus to more complex settings. Unit 4 - We explore various graphical applications. Unit 5 - We apply our techniques to solve real-world problems. We are very happy to have you in this course and look forward to working with you throughout the quarter! Watch this video that gives an overview of your MTH 252 Canvas course: Course Learning Outcomes By the end of this course, you should be able to: Describe the definite integral as a limit of Riemann sums and illustrate and interpret definite integrals as areas and signed areas. Evaluate integrals using basic numerical integration rules. Apply the fundamental theorem of calculus to evaluate integrals and to differentiate integrals with respect to a limit of integration. Use integration to find areas and volumes of regions and calculate physical quantities such as total distance traveled, displacement, work, and volume. Unit 5 - We apply our techniques to solve real-world problems. We are very happy to have you in this course and look forward to working with you throughout the quarter! Watch this video that gives an overview of your MTH 252 Canvas course: Course Learning Outcomes By the end of this course, you should be able to: Describe the definite integral as a limit of Riemann sums and illustrate and interpret definite integrals as areas and signed areas. Evaluate integrals using basic numerical integration rules. Apply the fundamental theorem of calculus to evaluate integrals and to differentiate integrals with respect to a limit of integration. Use integration to find areas and volumes of regions and calculate physical quantities such as total distance traveled, displacement, work, and volume. More to come.Posted on:Jun 26, 2026, 10:46 AM INTEGRAL CALCULUS (MTH_252Z_400_U2026) Front Page Welcome to MTH 252! --> For BOTH Sections 400 and 401 In this course we continue our study of Calculus. More specifically we will study, abstract, and apply the idea of measuring area between two curves. To group the content in a meaningful way, this course is split into five units: Unit 1 - We introduce Riemann sums as a tool to approximate area by summing up the area of rectangles. Unit 2 - We study the Fundamental Theorem of Calculus and related properties, which rely on "undoing" derivatives. Unit 3 - We study a variety of problem-solving techniques in order to apply the Fundamental Theorem of Calculus to more complex settings. Unit 4 - We explore various graphical applications. Unit 5 - We apply our techniques to solve real-world problems. We are very happy to have you in this course and look forward to working with you throughout the quarter! Watch this video that gives an overview of your MTH 252 Canvas course: Course Learning Outcomes By the end of this course, you should be able to: Describe the definite integral as a limit of Riemann sums and illustrate and interpret definite integrals as areas and signed areas. Evaluate integrals using basic numerical integration rules. Apply the fundamental theorem of calculus to evaluate integrals and to differentiate integrals with respect to a limit of integration. Use integration to find areas and volumes of regions and calculate physical quantities such as total distance traveled, displacement, work, and volume. pages.main_text_content: SEQUENCES AND SERIES (MTH_253Z_400_U2026) Front Page Course Overview Welcome to MTH 253Z! I am very happy to have you in this course and look forward to working with you throughout the quarter! In this course we will learn about infinite sequences and series. To group the content in a meaningful way, this course is split into five units: Unit 1 (Week 1) - In this unit, we will review indeterminate forms, L'Hospital's Rule, and improper integrals. Unit 2 (Weeks 2 and 3) - Here we will introduce sequences and series. What are they? How are they used? Unit 3 (Weeks 4, 5, and 6) - In this unit, we will learn how to test series for convergence or divergence using a number of different tests. Unit 4 (Weeks 7, 8, and 9) - This unit covers power series, including Taylor and Maclaurin series. Unit 5 (Week 10) - In this last unit, we will learn about applications of Taylor and Maclaurin series, approximating sums, complex series, and the Euler Identity. Final's Week Course Learning Outcomes By the end of this course, you should be able to: Recognize and define sequences in a variety of forms and describe their properties, including the concepts of convergence and divergence, boundedness, and monotonicity. Recognize and define series in terms of a sequence of partial sums and describe their properties, including convergence and divergence. Recognize series as harmonic, geometric, telescoping, alternating, or p-series, and demonstrate whether they are absolutely convergent, conditionally convergent, or divergent, and find their sum if applicable. Choose and apply the divergence, integral, comparison, limit comparison, alternating series, and ratio tests to determine the convergence or divergence of a series. Determine the radius and interval of convergence of power series, and use Taylor series to represent, differentiate, and integrate functions. Use techniques and properties of Taylor polynomials to approximate functions and analyze error. Start Here Syllabus Jump to a Unit:

pages.main_text_content: SEQUENCES AND SERIES (MTH_253Z_400_U2026) Front Page Course Overview Welcome to MTH 253Z! I am very happy to have you in this course and look forward to working with you throughout the quarter! In this course we will learn about infinite sequences and series. To group the content in a meaningful way, this course is split into five units: Unit 1 (Week 1) - In this unit, we will review indeterminate forms, L'Hospital's Rule, and improper integrals. Unit 2 (Weeks 2 and 3) - Here we will introduce sequences and series. What are they? How are they used? Unit 3 (Weeks 4, 5, and 6) - In this unit, we will learn how to test series for convergence or divergence using a number of different tests. Unit 4 (Weeks 7, 8, and 9) - This unit covers power series, including Taylor and Maclaurin series. Unit 5 (Week 10) - In this last unit, we will learn about applications of Taylor and Maclaurin series, approximating sums, complex series, and the Euler Identity. Final's Week Course Learning Outcomes By the end of this course, you should be able to: Recognize and define sequences in a variety of forms and describe their properties, including the concepts of convergence and divergence, boundedness, and monotonicity. Recognize and define series in terms of a sequence of partial sums and describe their properties, including convergence and divergence. Recognize series as harmonic, geometric, telescoping, alternating, or p-series, and demonstrate whether they are absolutely convergent, conditionally convergent, or divergent, and find their sum if applicable. Choose and apply the divergence, integral, comparison, limit comparison, alternating series, and ratio tests to determine the convergence or divergence of a series. Determine the radius and interval of convergence of power series, and use Taylor series to represent, differentiate, and integrate functions. Use techniques and properties of Taylor polynomials to approximate functions and analyze error. Start Here Syllabus Jump to a Unit:

pages.main_text_content: GENERAL PHYSICS WITH CALCULUS (PH_212_400_U2026) Home page PH 212 General Physics with Calculus . Welcome! This course is fully online. Lectures will be held via Zoom at a regularly scheduled time to be determined depending on students' availability. Zoom meeting information is posted in the Course Information module. Lecture videos are posted for those who cannot attend and asynchronous participation assignments are posted in Canvas. Labs are fully online, as well as the optional recitation course. There are alternate asynchronous assignments for all in-class activities. Quizzes and the final exam are delivered via Zoom at the regular Zoom lecture time and again at 6pm. Asynchronous alternatives for quizzes and the final exam are delivered via Proctorio. PH 212 covers a variety of topics including circular motion, rigid rotation, oscillations, waves, wave optics, ray optics and gravitation. Please make sure your Canvas settings are adjusted so that you receive announcements via email, so that you get information pertinent to the course. Please start by selecting the Modules menu button in the left pane and reading the material in the Course information module. Announcements Please check for announcements regularly to receive important course information. Select the Announcements menu button in the left pane to open the Announcements page. Announcements will also be sent to your ONID email account. Please check your Canvas settings to make sure notifications are turned on.

pages.main_text_content: GENERAL PHYSICS WITH CALCULUS (PH_212_400_U2026) Home page PH 212 General Physics with Calculus . Welcome! This course is fully online. Lectures will be held via Zoom at a regularly scheduled time to be determined depending on students' availability. Zoom meeting information is posted in the Course Information module. Lecture videos are posted for those who cannot attend and asynchronous participation assignments are posted in Canvas. Labs are fully online, as well as the optional recitation course. There are alternate asynchronous assignments for all in-class activities. Quizzes and the final exam are delivered via Zoom at the regular Zoom lecture time and again at 6pm. Asynchronous alternatives for quizzes and the final exam are delivered via Proctorio. PH 212 covers a variety of topics including circular motion, rigid rotation, oscillations, waves, wave optics, ray optics and gravitation. Please make sure your Canvas settings are adjusted so that you receive announcements via email, so that you get information pertinent to the course. Please start by selecting the Modules menu button in the left pane and reading the material in the Course information module. Announcements Please check for announcements regularly to receive important course information. Select the Announcements menu button in the left pane to open the Announcements page. Announcements will also be sent to your ONID email account. Please check your Canvas settings to make sure notifications are turned on.
